name: CMPKit Cookie Consent – GDPR Cookie Banner & Consent Mode v2
author: cmpkit

sections.description:
CMPKit Cookie Consent adds a cookie consent banner to your WordPress site. Paste your CMPKit site key and the banner appears: visitors can accept all, reject all, or choose categories (functional, analytics, marketing).

  • GDPR cookie banner with accept, reject and customize choices.
  • Google Consent Mode v2: Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager receive the visitor’s choice (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization).
  • WP Consent API: the choice is shared with WP Consent API, so compatible plugins only run what the visitor allowed.
  • Proof of consent: each choice is logged in your CMPKit dashboard.
  • Cookie settings button: visitors can reopen the panel and change their choice later (see the FAQ).
  • Lightweight: one small asynchronous script, no jQuery, no tracking of its own.

You need a free CMPKit account to get a site key (create one at cmpkit.com). The free plan covers small sites; the dashboard shows your usage. Scan your site to see which cookies it sets.

External service

This plugin loads a script from cmpkit.com (https://cmpkit.com/widget.js), a service by CMPKit, and the banner sends the visitor’s consent choice to cmpkit.com to keep the proof of consent. Terms of service: https://cmpkit.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://cmpkit.com/privacy. The plugin itself stores one option (the public site key) and no visitor data.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings > CMPKit and paste your site key (starts with cmpkit_).
sections.faq:
How can visitors change their cookie choices later?

Add a Custom HTML block to your footer (Appearance > Widgets or the Site Editor) with <button type="button" data-cmpkit="settings">Cookie settings</button>. Clicking it opens the CMPKit settings panel. See https://cmpkit.com/docs#platforms.
